one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible. I ordered takeaway and waited over 50 minutes. Awful, awful, awful, awful... They take way too long and it's empty, which is the worst part.
1+ hour

I ordered a burger combo through Uber Eats, paying extra for one of the burgers, which then arrived different from the one I ordered. And my daughter's dinner was completely burnt chicken fingers. Plus, the delivery driver waited an hour for the order. Awful.

We came all the way from Madrid just to eat here because the food is spectacular. We arrived at 3:47 pm and the waitress told us the kitchen was closed.

We pointed out that the hours on Google Maps said they closed at 5:00 pm, to which the response was that the manager had to change the hours and that the kitchen was closed. We tried to speak with the manager or the kitchen staff, but it was no use. We couldn't get takeout either because she insisted the kitchen was closed and that, obviously, the hours were what they were.

We understand the waitress's position and request that they change the hours to reflect the correct ones, as it's a shame that these kinds of situations occur, both for the customers and the service.

one_star_reviews.text: Terrible customer service. We arrived at 10:00 PM on a Sunday for dinner and were told they had no tables available, that they were all reserved, even though the place was practically 80% empty. I'm surprised everything was booked at that hour. Two days earlier, we arrived at 10:40 PM and they refused to serve us anything. When we told them we'd only have two coffees, they tried to offer us their most expensive dish as if we were fools. We immediately declined, and after a while, they insisted again, saying they could prepare something else for us, but it was too late. Because of these attitudes and actions, we were extremely dissatisfied with the service. If they don't want to work with the public, they should find another job.

I could go on and on, but it was a horrible experience, plain and simple. We ordered pizzas in 2017 and I'm still waiting for them in 2026. And then, after supposedly an hour and a half in the oven, they came out raw. On top of that, they mocked us and laughed in our faces. More

The menu prices have gone up, and the service has gone downhill considerably—it's outrageous. As a worker, I used to come here quite often when I was in the area; I'm afraid it'll be the last time. More

one_star_reviews.text: Do not park here. As soon as you enter the first floor, there are 3 cars with broken windows and full of glass.

I mentioned to you some time ago the importance of keeping the gates closed and controlling access to prevent unauthorized people from entering the parking garage. I pay a monthly fee precisely to have my car in a safer place and avoid situations like those that occur on the street.

Unfortunately, after what happened recently, with several vehicles having their windows smashed in theft, I believe my concern was more than justified.

I understand that no parking garage can guarantee absolute security, but I do expect that minimum measures will be taken to prevent or hinder unauthorized access and protect customers' vehicles.

It's true that this parking garage is the most convenient for me and that it's clean, but frankly, if it doesn't offer the security I'm paying for, I'll have to start considering other options that do give me the peace of mind I'm looking for when leaving my car here.

I hope you can take measures to prevent something like this from happening again.

one_star_reviews.text:
Booking is done via WhatsApp.
They give you the key at the restaurant, and you fill out the paperwork there, which they then leave lying around on a table in the bar. I saw other guests' information there. You can only pay in cash, and obviously, they don't even give you a receipt.
We stayed from Tuesday to Sunday, and I must add that they didn't clean the room for six days, they didn't empty the trash cans, they didn't replenish the toilet paper. We had to go to the bar to ask for it, and they gave us the paper on the street, next to the bar's storage room. They weren't even able to say, "We'll go and put it out ourselves."
At that point, I asked the same person in charge about the room cleaning, and she told us that if I wanted cleaning, it was an extra charge. I was stunned. I asked about the towel changes, and her response was that some people stay for a month and don't want towel changes, and that for the price of the room, what did I expect? The conversation was unbelievable. (They never changed our towels.)
The shower tray was awful, the smallest one on the market, and it even had a curtain, so all the water splashed out and you couldn't even bend down to wash your feet. Imagine the puddle of water in the bathroom every day after showering; the only towel on the floor was soaked from Tuesday to Sunday. We didn't even have access to a mop.

Finally, I should add that our room was right above the bar's kitchen. The cooks finished work at 1:30 a.m. and sat under our window listening to music and eating. I had to lean out at 2:00 a.m. to politely ask them to turn down the music and lower their voices, which they completely ignored. Half an hour later, I had to repeat the same request about the music and the voices. Zero rest!

Never again.

one_star_reviews.text:
🤦‍♀️ WHEN I STEPS ONTO BARAJAS AIRPORT:
Every time I set foot in that airport… something goes wrong. It's like they're saying, "What can we do to make things difficult for this person today?" That strange energy that greets you the moment you walk in.

🛩️ THE AIRPORT THAT CREATES PROBLEMS:
I've been to airports of all kinds… but Madrid's has a special knack for messing things up. And on top of that, each Spanish airport seems to have its own rules, as if they were independent kingdoms.

‼️ CUSTOMER SERVICE:
The customer service… is the worst. They don't listen, they don't help, they give you false information and wash their hands of it like Pontius Pilate.
You ask for help and they ignore you.

And I don't know how they do it, but it doesn't matter what month it is: they never know anything, they can never do anything, they never solve anything.
Maybe it's just that it always happens to coincide with when I go.

🤷‍♀️ SECURITY:
And when you have to deal with security… it's a whole other level. They ruin your trip before you even take off.

🛃 SECURITY IN “CATTLE” MODE:
And watch out 👀, the security guards… oh my god. Zero manners, they speak rudely to you, look down on you, zero empathy, zero humanity.
They treat you like cattle, literally. And there's always, ALWAYS, something wrong with them. It doesn't matter what time 🕢, what day 📅 it is.
Just sour faces 😡 and zero willingness to help. And it's not just at Barajas Airport; the one in Barcelona and a few others are no good either.

🛄 THE CHECKPOINT THAT'S ALWAYS LOOKING FOR TROUBLE:
You go through security and they always find something on you.

Suddenly, your creams have to go in a little bag, even though they have scanners that can see right through your suitcase… but apparently, they don't use them.

And in the end, they make you pay a fortune to check them in.

As if paying magically makes them cease to be a “danger.”

🗓️ IT ALL DEPENDS ON THE DAY:
It all depends on which agent you get and which security guard is on duty. It's like playing Russian roulette.

🤔 WAS IT NECESSARY?:
I don't know if it's the management, the staff, or the atmosphere of the place… but I always leave thinking: “Was all this really necessary?”

📣 I'M NOT THE ONLY ONE: I'm sharing this because I know I'm probably not the only one who leaves there with their patience completely exhausted.

A terrible experience!!!!
That there isn't a single bench within a 2 km radius of an airport with both domestic and international flights is a real disgrace. The best thing to do is arrive with nothing to lose and just board the plane. If you have to wait, pray and sit on the floor.

Thanks Ayuso and Almeida, you've handled the homeless situation efficiently.
I hope I never have to return.

one_star_reviews.text: I'm a regular customer, and today's experience was terrible. We ordered rice with carabineros prawns for €28 a portion—unbelievable!—and it had absolutely no flavor. We mentioned it, and the waiter told us the cook said it needed a little salt, unbelievable, and then brought out the salt shaker. The carabineros were the same—zero flavor. I'm from Alicante, so I know a bit about rice dishes, and it was truly bland. To top it off, we ordered aioli, which they usually bring without having to ask, and to our surprise, they charged us €1.30 for it—the first time I've ever seen that in Alicante. No bread, no lemon... anyway. The waiters were very poorly coordinated. You order a drink, and they tell you to ask a colleague? Which one? When? I hope they improve the food and service because I was extremely disappointed, although the terrace is wonderful.

Both of us agreed that the prawn rice was bland. It had no flavor. We told the waiter on duty (they all seemed clueless, to say the least) that he took a plate to the kitchen and brought it back after the chef's assessment… “It has flavor, but it needs salt.” Anyway… We asked for the salt shaker, and obviously, neither of us finished it.

They didn't care and didn't do anything to make amends (they even charged us for the measly shot of salt).

A place we won't be returning to.

By the way, across the street on the beach, you can find better rice dishes and cheaper ones. Oh well.

Our experience with Sergio Nieva has been very negative, and we feel it necessary to share it publicly.

Our relationship with Sergio began when, as a construction worker, he started doing some work on our property. Later, trusting him and trying to help him, we agreed that he could stay on the property in exchange for rent and the completion of certain construction work.

Unfortunately, the situation turned out to be completely different from what we had agreed upon.

After a very long time, we have finally managed to get the property back, and thankfully, he has now moved out. Upon entering, we found it in a state that required a thorough cleaning, with numerous defects, damage to various areas and installations, and unfinished construction work.

In addition to all this, there are outstanding rent and utility bills. The water bill alone is approximately €1,400, which we, as the owners, are responsible for. There are also significant outstanding amounts related to the electricity supply, which we are currently dealing with in the process of resolving with Iberdrola.

We have photographs and videos of the condition in which we recovered the property, as well as communications, invoices, and documentation related to the amounts and expenses we are claiming. We've posted some photos so anyone can see and assess the condition of the property when we found it.

But what's especially frustrating is that we're still trying to contact Sergio, and he's not answering our calls.

That's why I want to make this public here as well:

Sergio, if you read this review, please get in touch with us. We're still open to talking and for you to settle the outstanding amounts and cover any damages and expenses. We'd prefer this situation to be resolved responsibly.

Trusting and trying to help someone only to find ourselves in this situation has been deeply disappointing.

If we can't resolve this, we will continue to pursue our rights through the appropriate legal channels.

Everything described here is based on our personal experience, and we have documentation regarding the facts and amounts we are claiming.

one_star_reviews.text:
Delivery times not respected, more than 3 weeks to receive my order with no communication from the seller.
Two boxes were completely broken.
Impossible to contact customer service, which never answers the phone.
Avoid at all costs! I placed another order, still not delivered.

Absolutely appalling customer experience

We ordered tile samples in July as part of our kitchen project, intending to place a much larger order afterward.

There was no delivery tracking, no code received to collect the package, no notification of availability or even return. On the Ceramic Connection website, the delivery status remained unchanged. Despite several follow-ups from us trying to find out where the package was, customer service finally replied, after stating that the order hadn't even been shipped, that it had already been returned to the sender.

And then, to our astonishment: we were told that since the carrier had completed their task, the delivery costs remained our responsibility and that we simply had to place a new order for samples and pay the shipping costs again.

Yet we never received the package, never received a code to collect it, and were never informed that it was available!

When we reported this obvious failure on the part of the carrier, Ceramic Connection told us they were opening an investigation. Ten days later, still no news, no explanation, and above all, no solution.

All this for a simple sample order placed in July…

The problem isn't even solely with the carrier anymore: it's the way Ceramic Connection is handling the situation that's truly incomprehensible. No serious follow-up, no real support, no goodwill gesture, and in the end, the customer has to bear the consequences of a malfunction for which they bear absolutely no responsibility.

Such disastrous handling of a sample order obviously doesn't inspire any enthusiasm for entrusting them with a much larger tile order in the future.

A friend recommended this garage to me, saying they were good at working on Abarths, and despite the distance—about 60 kilometers—I decided to go there. They weren't the cheapest of the quotes I received, and now, seeing the mistakes they made, they seem almost expensive.

In my case, it was a timing belt kit, spark plugs, and the turbo manifold hose. I picked up the car, and when I got home, the coolant level was well below the minimum in the expansion tank. I had to buy coolant and top it up, and they told me to bring it back the next day for a check. I took it back, and they saw that they simply hadn't completely filled the expansion tank. But hey, it happens... On the other hand, they replaced the turbo manifold hose, but they left several clamps on. Two mistakes are too many... For what I paid, the work left a lot to be desired, and I'm not going to make another 120-kilometer trip just to get two clamps. I'll find them myself. I'm very disappointed with this workshop. I don't recommend it.

Overpriced

I went to this garage because my car had an oil leak. They inspected the car and gave me a list of repairs they said needed to be done. After the repairs, I paid almost €800.

They told me I should then bring the car in for an engine cleaning (an additional €40) and return to the garage to find out where the oil was still leaking from and fix the problem.

I went back after the cleaning, and since then, they've just kept putting me off. Now they've given me another appointment and want me to leave the car there for a week so they can recheck everything.

What I find completely unacceptable is having paid almost €800 for repairs, in addition to the engine cleaning, and that after all this, the problem I brought the car in for is still not fixed.

If they couldn't properly determine or fix the cause of the oil leak from the beginning, they should have explained it clearly before carrying out the repairs and charging that amount.

My experience so far has been very disappointing, and above all, I feel like I'm wasting time and money trying to get them to fix a problem that should already be resolved.

one_star_reviews.text:
The points in the "Terms and Conditions" section of the Replus website seem outrageous to me. The factory washes its hands of the matter and shirks its responsibility regarding the warranty of the products it manufactures. What happens if the supplier of one of its retail outlets goes bankrupt and disappears? Who honors the warranty on the windows, for example? Can't customers contact another supplier at one of its retail outlets to claim the warranty?
This is something to be wary of.

Pay close attention to point "3. Absence of contractual responsibility" in the Terms and Conditions of use section of the website.

It's a very clever way for REPLUS to evade responsibility, to wash their hands of the matter.

If the company managing one of their "Points of Sale" disappears, or if the end customer loses confidence in that company and doesn't want to deal with them, there's no procedure for enforcing the product warranty.

That's what happened to us. We had all our exterior windows and doors installed by REPLUS, and now we have a problem with one of them. Since we don't trust the company that did the installation, and it has also moved (it's no longer at the REPLUS Point of Sale where we made the purchase), we wanted to resolve the issue with the company that's now at the same Point of Sale, but they tell us it's not possible.

In short, we've been left without the warranty that the windows should have.

I left my wedding shoes with him. They were originally white, but they were stained (beige), and when he returned them, they were still beige. That's fine by me. If I leave you shoes to be made white and you can't do it, at least DON'T CHARGE ME €15 if you don't know how or can't do the job. Or at least, if you don't know how they'll turn out (which is most likely), don't charge me the full amount for the service.

Photo 1. New shoes. How they look white.

Photo 2. The shoes after the wedding, covered in sand from the garden where it was held.

Photo 3. The shoes he returned to me after cleaning. How can they be beige instead of white as they were originally?

Not recommended at all.

I worked at this company for seven years, and this review reflects only my personal experience during that time.

Initially, the atmosphere was good, but over the last few years, I witnessed a considerable change. In my experience, the pressure on employees increased, the treatment of staff worsened, and the work environment became increasingly negative. During my final period there, I saw several colleagues decide to leave, which I personally perceived as a sign of the discontent that existed.

I find it regrettable how much I changed after so many years with the company.

And I believe it's unfair that the opinions of former employees are silenced simply because they worked there. This is my experience, my perception, and my opinion, and I believe I have the right to share it respectfully and honestly, just like anyone else.

I don't intend to speak for anyone else. I'm only speaking about what I experienced during my seven years working there.

one_star_reviews.text:
The Official College of Psychologists functions less as a health regulatory body and more as a corporatist guild designed to shield the mediocrity of its members. You pay your dues, they give you the seal of approval, and from then on, the patient is completely unprotected against any malpractice.
Protection of the professional, defenselessness of the patient.
If a doctor makes a mistake, there is objective evidence. Here, the ethics committee is a bulwark that protects the therapist by default. If a member decides to talk on the phone in the middle of a paid session at a specialist's rate, or if, faced with a hostile environment of workplace bullying, their main intervention is to recommend "joining a cooking club," the College will look the other way. And if the user demands the basic respect that would be expected of any other service, the professional always has the institutional trump card to invalidate the complaint by questioning "how the patient manages their emotions."

Facade Science and Zero Audits
They demand the status, authority, and fees of medical science, but they play by the rules of an unregulated market. There are no biomarkers, no guarantees, and no one monitors the success or failure rates of registered professionals. The system protects so-called experts who substitute the scientific method with moral superiority, personal biases, and barroom advice disguised as therapy.

An Untouchable Business Model
The College's only visible concern is cracking down on unqualified practitioners to protect its coffers, maintaining a deafening silence about its own internal incompetence. They allow and whitewash an abusive business model that thrives on exploiting vulnerable people, fostering weekly dependency instead of offering practical solutions. When the supposed therapy fails due to adverse material realities, the entire system supports the psychologist in washing their hands of the matter and blaming the client for not trying hard enough.

As long as they continue to operate as a vertical syndicate that exempts its members from all accountability, their title of "evidence-based therapy" will remain a mere slogan to justify a legalized macro-fraud.

one_star_reviews.text:
If you want to survive an emergency, you're better off going to another hospital, because in this one they not only look at you with contempt and arrogance, I'd love to know the names of the "nurses"—if you can even call them that, since it seems like they just hand out the title... We arrived with suspected drug intoxication, and on top of that, when they asked if she'd been drinking and we told them two drinks, which is practically nothing, they made a gesture as if to say, "That means she's drunk." We waited two damn hours to be seen, and in the meantime, the girl started having tremors, pain in her arm, and chills, and they gave us a damn filthy sheet, saying, "Here, cover it up and that's it."
Once we got into the cubicles, there were two nurses drawing blood from each other, making comments like, "My God, how hard they're making me work this last hour!" It's incredible how my face looked watching and listening to them because I went twice to ask for a change of IV drip. When I finally returned to the cubicle with my colleague, a patient started calling out, and one of the nurses, without hesitation, loudly declared, "Oh my God, here comes that pest again!"
Ladies, if you don't have the vocation, don't do it and make way for competent people. I find it unbelievable that these people have positions in a hospital when they are so despicable and lack empathy.

one_star_reviews.text: A horrible, nightmare-like experience. The doctor treated me in a terrible mood because, according to him, it wasn't my assigned hospital. I was assigned to another one, but I went there because I know they're well-known for urinary tract infections, which I'd been suffering from for four months. I absolutely do not recommend it unless you were prepared to spend all morning and afternoon waiting only to leave feeling the same or worse than when you arrived.

Doctors completely disillusioned with their profession, offering no explanations and lacking empathy; doctors totally indifferent to the patient; cases they label as very rare, treated with disinterest and apathy. Thanks to several letters to the administration, I finally got a testicular biopsy, which revealed a neoplasm. This biopsy had been previously denied by the center "because I didn't have a partner," which wasn't part of the protocol. I'm 35 years old. They didn't deem it appropriate to freeze my sperm when I was diagnosed with a varicocele in my early twenties. The varicocele surgery was also performed after several insistences and letters to the administration on my part. The biopsy revealed azoospermia and a neoplasm (I underwent radiotherapy at St. Paul's Hospital). If it had been up to the center, it would never have been detected or treated. My brother had a similar case years ago, but he didn't undergo genetic testing. This center's lack of interest in the patient is blatant.

Horrible experience with a TURP scheduled through the public healthcare system. I went to the emergency room four times because I couldn't urinate, and they completely ignored me. After almost three months, I finally saw the urologist who performed the surgery, and he didn't even examine me and dismissed me in 20 seconds, I'm telling you. If I had known, I wouldn't have had this surgery at this clinic in a million years.

one_star_reviews.text:
❌❌❌ VERY NEGATIVE REVIEW ❌❌❌

I want to share our experience with this agency because we felt completely deceived. They promised us a clean, renovated, and move-in-ready home, but when they gave us the keys, we found a filthy house in completely unacceptable condition.

The house had previously been a workshop, which was clearly evident from the blue, holey, and burnt floors. The kitchen was completely dirty and dilapidated, the bathroom was filthy, the floors had shoe prints, the sofa smelled of mold, and there was a strong odor of mildew and dampness throughout the house. The beds were covered in stains and smelled so bad that it was impossible to even think about sleeping there.

The worst part is that we had already seen the house before and had clearly stated that we couldn't live in those conditions. They promised that they would change practically everything and that they had done a lot of work.

We signed the contract before even seeing the property again because our roommates had previously rented another place through him and trusted him, considering him, in a manner of speaking, almost a friend. We trusted his promises and didn't see the property again before moving in.
They gave us the keys the same morning we moved in, and that's when we discovered the reality. Virtually nothing had changed. The only difference was some lamps with fans because there wasn't even air conditioning.
Furthermore, we still have photos and videos of the condition we found the house in.
We tried calling the agency many times, but no one answered. We had to go there in person, and they told us they couldn't waste their time because they were working, as if we weren't clients.
Then they told us, "Don't worry, we'll bring you new beds this afternoon." We had already rented a van and put all our clothes and belongings inside the house. They left us waiting on the street until 7:00 PM, and the beds never arrived. We tried contacting them from 7:00 PM until 11:00 PM. They finally called us back saying they couldn't do anything and that, according to them, the house was perfectly clean and that they had even cleaned it themselves.

Can you really call a house "spotless" when it has a dirty, run-down kitchen, a filthy bathroom, floors covered in shoe prints, beds covered in stains, a sofa that smells of mold, and a strong musty odor throughout the house?
I also have a serious chronic illness; I'm asthmatic and allergic to dust and mold, so these conditions are no joke to me.
They told us that if the house wasn't up to our standards, we could go back to the agency and they would refund our deposit. That night we had to sleep in a B&B. The next day we loaded all our things back into the van and went back to the agency. Finally, they returned our deposit.

Then we wasted three days looking for another place to live, in addition to the money, time, and stress we had already lost. Luckily, we found a completely different agency: incredibly kind and helpful people who assisted us immediately and showed us into a beautiful, spotless house where we could finally breathe fresh air and live with dignity.
I've never seen an agency like this or such behavior. I absolutely do not recommend this agency. Be extremely careful before trusting them and paying a fortune only to find yourself in a home in these conditions.

A terrible experience. Never again.

one_star_reviews.text: SCAMMERS!!! They quoted you €1500 for a repair I rejected, and another mechanic fixed it for €300. When you have an official Hyundai under warranty, you have two problems: they deny the warranty on some illegal technicality and then give you a repair estimate of almost €1500!!! But you reject it because it seems outrageous. They force you to pay €100 for the diagnosis, and then another mechanic fixes everything legally for €300. That's the only word they deserve: SCAMMERS. Run away from that place.

Four years ago, we bought a Hyundai Kona because, due to technical problems with our previous car (the turbo and engine failed due to a manufacturing defect in a 2016 Range Rover), we had to get a temporary, but new, car. I say temporary because it's not the model we like, but we could have it in a month. We agreed with the salesman that we could return it after four years by paying the final installment. This year, 2026, the problems started. Hyundai Spain washed their hands of all the dealerships in the province of Barcelona, ​​since those in Barcelona city had been closing. They told us we could finalize the purchase with them at a dealership in Castelldefels (they hadn't worked with Hyundais for over a year), but we ended up at one in Sant Boi. The worst. The service was terrible; they treated us badly and even said they weren't going to take responsibility. Even without checking the mileage, which would have been a major problem if we'd gone over 40,000 km... no way we had that many. Then they said it wasn't their problem, that if we kept another Hyundai, fine, but returning it was out of the question. Finally, they said they'd call us on July 6th to appraise it and see what could be done. I made four calls to the salesperson to get them to call me back, but nothing. Then we contacted Hyundai Spain again, as the return date was approaching. We tried the dealership in Badalona. We called. The guy's response: "Oh no, we're not going to take it, it's not our problem. You have to sell it yourself and then pay the final installment. You'll get more money, and besides, if we appraised it, it would be for less." There was only a week left until the final payment. It seems unbelievable, total stress because we couldn't keep two cars. We sold it and paid it off. The financial settlement wasn't quick either. In short, lots of promises and nothing but problems when it comes down to it. I absolutely do not recommend this brand. The customer service is terrible, practically nonexistent; they're arrogant and I imagine they only fawn over you if you switch to another model after four years. There are much better options on the market.

Have all manners disappeared? What is this, the exit from a circus? Are we on some third-world catwalk? I mean, seriously, can't they just stick to THEIR STAND without HARASSING people? Yes, literally harassing. Sometimes they even follow you. This is harassment. There are ways and ways to treat people. But please, do something! At least teach them some basic manners and that's it. They should stick to their stall, their line of business. Let people walk around peacefully and eat; don't follow me. Besides, it gives a shabby, desperate, cheap, low-quality, and third-world image. How pathetic... Get rid of the "flea market" stalls!

I go to that shopping center a lot; it's usually a very pleasant place where you can shop, eat, have a drink, or just stroll around. My bad rating stems from the opening of one of their new restaurants (Bobbi's, I think). From 12:30 to 1:00 pm onwards, it's unbearable to be in the food court near this restaurant. They fill the whole floor with smoke and smells. I can't eat at Ginos, have a drink at Haguen, Montaditos, or Frutolandia without my eyes burning or the smell of the air being more noticeable than the food itself. They shouldn't allow so much smoke to be generated without a good extraction system. Both the shopping center and the restaurant are to blame. If the shopping center doesn't want to install extractors, they should force the restaurant to do so.
I don't think it's very healthy to breathe inside a shopping center where the ventilation air outlet is like that.
I don't recommend it for parking because if you don't spend the amount they stipulate, they still charge you for parking. I don't recommend the shopping center in general.
Zero professionalism

one_star_reviews.text:
One August afternoon, and at first glance, everything seemed perfect: a pool with great views, delicious cocktails, a relaxed atmosphere, and fairly decent food.

But then the paella arrived… and the drama began.

After the appetizers, we waited an hour and a half. We were waiting for the paella, and the paella, it seemed, was on vacation. Finally, the waitress appeared, asking if we wanted dessert. Dessert? Ma'am, we're still waiting for the main course!

It turns out they'd forgotten to send it away. And instead of offering to cancel it, they told us to wait a little longer. By then, our appetites were practically packing their bags.

Finally, the paella arrived. And we wanted to speak to the manager. After about ten minutes talking to the kitchen staff, he gave us a €13 discount. The discount was fine, but there was zero empathy, zero apology, and zero intention of understanding our frustration. His coldness made it seem as if he was the one who'd been waiting an hour and a half.

And it's a shame, because they have excellent food and a very nice setting. But when management fails like this, it's like having a Ferrari and putting wheelbarrow wheels on it: no matter how good the car is, you end up talking about the wheels.
Group size
2 people

My experience at this field was negative, very negative, because the person (the woman with glasses) who runs the bar treated me and my friends very badly, with constant disrespect, aggression, and rudeness. We've been consuming drinks all morning, and even so, she didn't tell us to go to the stands, speaking with no manners whatsoever. I think it's very wrong and unprofessional that she wouldn't order more drinks after we'd been there all morning. Excuse me? That's awful, and not just drinks, but sandwiches too! Oh! She told us that the next day when we come back, we shouldn't spend all morning at the table. Huh?! What kind of world do we live in? If she doesn't know how to run a bar, she should keep her bitterness at home. She's rude, and another thing, she changes the prices whenever she feels like it. And don't ask her for ice because she gets angry, saying it costs money too. My son-in-law ordered two colas and asked for a glass with ice, and then he went to play. After he finished playing, about 15 minutes later, my daughter-in-law came and asked for a glass with ice because it was warm. She told her she'd already given him one, and he replied that she'd ordered two colas and she'd given him a glass... Helloooooo, what's wrong with that lady...??? Well, we didn't like the service; she's bitter, and we customers aren't to blame for anything... We'll go tomorrow, but we'll shop at the Mercadona outside the camp, and they're more polite and not ungrateful. And everything's fine with the camp. 👎🏼👎🏼😡

I'm giving it one star, not for the facilities, but for the bar in the countryside, run by a bitter woman who treats her customers badly, with constant disrespect, rudeness, and aggression. In general, I encourage you to go to Mercadona if you want to buy anything, because it seems she doesn't know how to deal with people. On the other hand, I thought the facilities were very good.

I'm sorry when I have to give a negative review, but in this case, I'm giving one, AND I'LL JUSTIFY IT.

I'm studying osteopathy and therefore have NO experience. My professors recommended this company for my first treatment table, and I bought a portable model that they advertise on their website as suitable for osteopathy.

After eight months of studying and seeing that I wasn't getting the techniques right and didn't understand why, I consulted my professors, renowned osteopaths at the European level, and they asked me to show them the table I had. It turned out that the table is not suitable for applying osteopathic techniques for the thoracic spine, lumbar spine, ribs, etc., because it's too high and the padding is excessive.

After politely contacting the company, the only solution they offered was to cut the legs off the treatment table and leave the padding as is... WITH ALL EXPENSES PAID OUT OF MY OWN EXPENSES, €120 PLUS SHIPPING....

I wasn't expecting a free new treatment table, but I don't know... your solution for a customer who bought a product you advertise as suitable for a particular specialty, and then it turns out it ISN'T... I find it APPALLING.

BAD, BAD, BAD. Now I have a treatment table worth almost €500 that I don't need. A real joke.

one_star_reviews.text: I don't understand how a state-run public entity allows a private company (and a Dutch one at that, not even local) to operate on its premises, privatizing something that, in Maslow's hierarchy of needs, is the most basic human need: physiological needs. I was with my two daughters, who couldn't hold it any longer, and they demanded I pay 2 euros even though I wasn't going to use the restroom and we had our train tickets in hand. This all happened after my wife took the girls to the restroom and didn't have her wallet or card with her. When she explained it to me, I couldn't believe it. Next time, I'll let the girls do what they need to do at the company entrance and call the police; let's see who they side with when they arrive. It's a complete rip-off by Adif to allow this. I don't understand how this company has been operating on Joaquín Sorolla Street for so many years without the people of Valencia putting pressure on them to remove it. If we continue like this, we'll be forced to put coins in playgrounds for water and charged for breathing "premium" pollutant-free air in the city. Just you wait. To those of you from Valencia, I urge you to put a stop to this nonsense.

1euro!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
And then the toilet seat is covered in pee!
I find it regrettable that ADIF allows physiological needs to be monetized, and that a company like this is dedicated to profiting from it.

I find it unacceptable that at a train station like Joaquín Sorolla, the restrooms are closed first thing in the morning, when there are already passengers using the station and boarding trains.

And, what's more, when they are available, you have to pay to use them. I find it completely unacceptable that such a basic service as being able to use the restroom at a train station requires payment.

If you have an emergency, what do you do? A train station should guarantee minimum services to passengers, especially during operating hours.

Unacceptable. A station of this kind should take much better care of something so basic.

one_star_reviews.text:
A very bad experience with Global Exchange at Madrid-Barajas Airport. I went there to collect a Tax Free refund from Global Blue and specifically requested to receive my money in euros. The staff told me I could only receive it in dollars, which meant accepting a currency conversion I hadn't requested. I preferred to decline the cash and arrange for a refund to my card later.

Furthermore, the service was unpleasant and disrespectful, with extremely long queues and unclear information about the available refund options.

A Tax Free service at an international airport should provide transparent information about available currencies, exchange rates, and any fees before the traveler agrees to the transaction.

My experience was terrible, and I have filed a complaint.

Please pay your tax-free allowance by card 💳, not in cash.
My tax-free allowance in Euros was 29, and they gave me 15 dollars.
It's practically theft. You do it in a hurry after waiting an hour or more, thinking it's better than nothing.

But then you get home and think, "Scammers robbed me with that change!" When you pay your tax-free allowance by card, they give you a cheap rate, but they don't steal from you as blatantly as they do at the Global Blue office in Madrid-Barajas Airport near Terminal 4. It's close to the Diva machine where you verify all your receipts. If you can, it's better to use the Guardia Civil's tax-free service; it's near the restrooms. At least if they steal from you, it goes to the country and not to a malicious company.
Absolutely nightmarish. Too little associates, sero empathy, complicated system. One of the worst services I have experienced in my life.

Attention! It's important to insist on being paid tax-free in euros. The exchange rate they use for converting to other currencies is extremely unfavorable. Sometimes they ask for more euros to round off the amount, which means you're essentially buying dollars with euros at a rate of 0.83. The euro is more expensive than the dollar, and these people have it backwards. They take advantage of travelers who are happy to receive money but anxious about missing their flights, doing whatever they want, and most people fall for their scams.

Thanks for trying to fool me!

What a wonderfully suspicious experience... I went to claim my Tax Free refund and asked for it in euros (yes, the local currency, nothing unusual). But no, the friendly representative confidently explained that since I'm not a resident, they couldn't pay me in euros, only in dollars. How curious, right?

I politely asked if he could show me which European law this policy is based on. Spoiler alert: no such law exists. And then, as if by magic...voilà!

It turns out they could pay me in euros after all.
What a marvel of service: first they misinform you, then they charge you for their "mistake," and if you insist with evidence, they magically change their minds. It's like a tax escape room: if you don't ask the right questions, you lose.

So if you're reading this and they offer you dollars when you ask for euros, smile, say "no, thank you," and do what I did: ask for the law in writing. It works better than any magic trick.

Tip for the business: Keep up this original technique; it's sure to bring you many reviews like this one.

Tip for travelers: Always ask for prices in euros and demand transparency!

one_star_reviews.text:
Don't go!

On Sunday, August 30, 2026, we went to this place full of excitement. We had high expectations. What a shame about the dismissive and arrogant treatment we received from the two girls who work there. Let me tell you. While we were in the jacuzzi, someone mistakenly took our towels. When we went to ask for new towels, these two employees not only complained about why we hadn't been paying attention to them (I think the reason is obvious ;-) ), but in a very unfriendly tone, they demanded we pay €4 for the new towels (the problem wasn't paying, but their incredibly unprofessional treatment).

With no other option, we told them we would pay before leaving. They angrily replied that we wouldn't, and that we should read the Spa rules written on one of the walls! Rules we didn't even know existed because during the rushed welcome tour one of them gave us, she never explained them or asked us to read them.

Imagine the scene. We stood there, exposed, in front of the bar, freezing cold and confused by what was happening, while the hostesses showed absolutely no interest in helping us.

When we told one of them that we disliked their hostile attitude, the other replied that they weren't there to be our friends! They never had the slightest intention of listening to us. All they did was justify their mistreatment by hiding behind the empty phrase they kept repeating, "We were polite and respectful." You can be disrespectful without swearing.

We all have bad days. Maybe they were tired, or in a bad mood from working on a Sunday. But does that justify the mistreatment of two customers who were visiting the spa for the first time?
We left soaked and disappointed. I hope the spa management provides their employees with training in customer empathy. Those little details are what make the difference between a bad experience and an unforgettable one.

one_star_reviews.text:
Beware! Everyone should know what to expect from this insurance. This is my opinion based on my own experience with this company.
Numerous attempts to unilaterally, unjustifiably, and without prior agreement to collect funds, and a complete lack of regard for the client's interests.
I want to warn prospective clients about the management methods of this AXA office so they can assess the true costs before signing a contract.
I officially notified them of my intention not to renew my health insurance policy more than seven months in advance, despite my strict adherence to all deadlines. Because some of the insured parties on my policy had left the country, I notified the agency in writing that, given their departure, I requested that the declaration of non-renewal be considered valid for them, and that my policy remain in effect only on the condition of maintaining the previous individual cost of the insurance (especially since the insurer is obligated to notify of any cost change two months in advance of the proposed renewal). At the same time, the same written notification stated that, in the event of a unilateral increase in the cost for me, the contract would be considered terminated and would NOT be renewed.

The agency concealed the final individual cost from me until the very last day of the policy's expiration date, attempting to unilaterally apply a rate increase that doubled my original cost, without the legally required two-month notice, as stipulated in Article 22 of the Insurance Contract Law.

After I rejected this unjustifiable increase and terminated the contract in a timely manner, the agent informed me in writing that it was easier for him not to process the administrative cancellation and to allow the system to issue receipts so that the contract would be canceled due to "non-payment," attempting to shift the blame to the client and cover up his record. Consequently, I filed a complaint regarding the agent's actions at the end of June at atencion.clientes@axa.es, to which, two months later, no one has responded at all.

Currently, in September, with the contract already expired, the company's system has attempted to withdraw money from my account four times, apparently to circumvent the restrictions and the cancellation of the direct debit I set up with my bank, through a method I did not authorize.

This has forced me to constantly monitor my balance and manually reverse the payments repeatedly.
Customer service does not respond to official written complaints within 30 days, as was the case with mine. Entering into a contract with this agency carries the risk of constant stress and the loss of a significant amount of personal time verifying accounts, reversing unauthorized payments, and drafting complaints. This is time and effort that will likely never be compensated. This appears to be an unbearable contract management practice and a complete lack of respect for the customer.
Overall, I strongly advise against doing business with this company, especially for those who have little time to constantly monitor their accounts. If they suddenly thought they could cancel and delete the contract at the bank, it won't work that way because, by all accounts, they seem to change the order of collection and, despite the block, try to collect the funds through a single payment, as well as from pensioners with poor eyesight, for example, or people with disabilities, who may simply not realize this.

I purchased a phone case for a company phone and specifically asked if they could provide a company invoice. They said, "No problem."

After two months, five calls, and three visits to the store—where the manager is never present—I'm still waiting for the invoice. They've been passing the buck: first, they said the manager wasn't there; then, it was a matter for headquarters; and finally (a week ago), they said they were sending it.

It's harder to issue a €20 invoice than to break into NASA.

I've given up. I won't be back, and I don't recommend anyone go there if they need business-level customer service.

I went in for a phone case and a screen protector. I said I was looking for an anti-spy screen protector, but they didn't show it to me first, nor did they tell me if they had a variety. They just put it on automatically without even asking if that's what I was looking for. On top of that, the protector isn't even made of glass or anything like that; it's a flexible plastic, and they don't tell you that at any point.

I'm giving it one star because I can't give it less. We ended up leaving the store without being able to buy what we needed. As soon as we arrived, the two employees were chatting away at the register. I waited to be served, and the girl couldn't advise us. We spent a while trying to figure out what size we needed, but they completely ignored us, and we left the store without buying what we needed. If this is how they work, great. I absolutely do not recommend this store.

I had a screen protector installed less than two weeks ago, and it's already peeling off at the corners just from daily use. This is the second time it's happened. Poor quality product for the price (it's not cheap).

My experience on August 13, 2026, at 6:00 PM was by far the worst I've had in many years. I fly about six to eight times a year, and I've never encountered such a disrespectful person as the one supervising his colleagues that day.

He lied on several occasions, constantly interrupting me so I couldn't express my point of view on the conflict that stole 15 minutes of my time, my family's time, and the time of the long line that had formed behind me. I know they take advantage of that, but there's a big difference between that and embarrassing themselves in front of the other passengers. To top it all off, I was charged more than the amount on the bill I received several days later, not before he tried to humiliate me by checking that my backpack fit in the overhead bin, a process I carried out without complaint and successfully.

I'm still in dispute with them and with Wizzair. I'm going to claim a refund for the difference between what I paid and what I was billed, and I'm going to look for alternatives like Air Serbia to fly to the Balkans in the future.

one_star_reviews.text: Without getting into the pointless argument about the store's exorbitant prices... I'd like to mention the rude, arrogant, and condescending attitude of the short-haired employee—she's from Granada, by the way. She looks at you like you're a second-class citizen and answers you even worse. All because I didn't realize my receipt was face down on the counter. In my opinion, there are surely many young people in the area with beautiful smiles and the typical friendliness of the locals, eager to learn and treat people like human beings. Even though the prices almost demand it, all you ask for is to be treated as an equal. A year and a few liters that will never be from this station again.

This is the first and last time I've stopped for coffee. The girl who works at the café leaves much to be desired. First, she ignores you while talking to her colleague for several minutes, and when I ask where I can order a coffee, she tells me here, but that she's serving someone else. I keep waiting, and there's no one she's serving or attending to. In the end, I leave without getting my coffee. Very bad service and a lack of enthusiasm for her work. And the best part is that I go to the gas station to ask if they serve coffee there, and the girl who works there was sweeping outside. I greet her, and she doesn't even look at me or leave. I go inside to wait, as does another girl who was also waiting, and she continues sweeping as if we don't exist for several minutes. Really bad, honestly. I won't be coming back here.

Don't even think about stopping here! The employees are unpleasant and inefficient. I stopped to refuel and left the pump connected. After a few seconds, it stalled. I tried to pump it myself, and it stalled again. I told her, but she completely ignored me. I went to my car to check if I hadn't accidentally pumped the wrong pump. The pump wasn't working. I saw that the tank was only half full. By then, she still hadn't paid any attention. I went back, even angrier, but she still ignored me. After a while, she came back, mumbled something, and started pumping from empty (I was careful enough to take a picture of the pump's condition). Now, 15 or 16 minutes later, and still no explanation. I have to do the math because she won't tell me anything at all. I think it's fine that they bring people from elsewhere to work here if the positions aren't filled with locals, but they should leave their bad coffee at home. Anyway, most of the places on the Mudejar highway are unacceptable.

UNACCEPTABLE PRACTICES AT AN OFFICIAL SERVICE CENTER AND DEGRADING TREATMENT.

I want to warn other users about the practices of Bétula Cars (an official Citroën workshop in Ourense). We took my partner's car there for a turbo repair, and it was damaged in an accident while they were on their premises. Far from acting honestly, they didn't inform us of anything and tried to cover up the damage by installing a used headlight with visible signs of wear and a code painted on the lens with a blue marker. Furthermore, they returned the car to us with a misalignment that causes the passenger door to rub when opened.
For an official workshop to commit such a serious act as to damage a customer's car, conceal it, and secretly "fix" it with used parts seems to me not only a crime but also a disgrace.

After much insistence, the car had to be taken back to their workshop to rectify the damage.

We've already picked it up, but the handling of the situation has been appalling right up to the last minute: they didn't even notify us when it was ready, and from the very first contact, every communication has been solely due to our insistence. They've admitted what happened, but we've never received a single apology from them. A lack of professionalism unworthy of the brand they represent.

one_star_reviews.text:
If you're thinking of moving to this town with your family, consider carefully whether you're willing to sacrifice your peace and quiet. There's a hidden side to the town's historical charm that goes unmentioned:

In recent years, it has become a party destination for many young people from Valencia, who come up on weekends to drink in public, have a good time, and return home on Sunday, leaving broken windows as if the town were a playground.

The town council, far from taking action, exploits the phenomenon, since tourism is Jérica's main economic driver. The celebration of patron saint festivals (and any other celebration, of which there are many) gives free rein to those who celebrate by setting off fireworks at 1 AM and marching with drums at 6 AM. Respect for residents and families is conspicuously absent.

The announcements are made over loudspeakers several times a day, from 8 AM until nightfall. Water service interruption notices (1 or 2 per week on average), police notices to owners of illegally parked vehicles, announcements from the festival committee, death notices...

I'm writing this after spending sleepless nights waking my one-and-a-half-year-old son multiple times, while also being nine months pregnant.

Therefore, I reiterate that Jérica is not a family destination where you would raise your children. If you're looking for peace and quiet, my advice is to keep searching and visit the town if you enjoy weekend getaways, keeping in mind that it's primarily a town of second homes and seasonal tourism.

one_star_reviews.text: THESE PEOPLE ARE OUT OF THEIR MINDS!! We arrived, took a table, and I asked the waiter if the table was reserved. The guy looked at me and, without even greeting me, said: "It's not that I'm bored at home and have nothing to do, that's why I come here!!" IS THIS HOW THEY TREAT PEOPLE IN THIS PLACE?

It's a shame to have to write this review because we've been coming to this restaurant for years and have always loved it. Furthermore, both the waiter who served us on Saturday and on other occasions, as well as the waitress, have been charming and very professional.

After our meal and finishing our coffees and desserts, we ordered a drink, and before ordering a second one, a woman—we don't know her position within the restaurant, whether she's a manager, head waitress, or owner—approached us and said, "I have to bring you the bill; I need the table." We replied that we were planning to order another drink and that we weren't finished yet. Her response was, "You have to leave; I have a lot of people waiting. Besides, you came without a reservation."

We completely understand that they need a table for a second seating, but the fact that we came without a reservation is irrelevant. If the restaurant gave us a table and no one informed us that there was a time limit, we shouldn't have to know their internal procedures.

And, above all, there are ways and ways to handle these situations. We can't say she was rude, but she certainly acted quite inappropriately. She could have explained that they needed the table and offered to move us to the bar or the terrace, both of which are available. Even if there weren't any free tables outside at that moment, they could have offered us a seat at the bar and moved us when one became available. And if there really wasn't any possibility, it would have been enough to say it politely: "I'm sorry, I've been looking into it and we can't find a new table for you." Very different from a blunt "you have to leave."

When we expressed our dissatisfaction and mentioned that, after so many years of coming here, we wouldn't be returning, she brought the bill and said, "I'm truly sorry if this has upset you." Precisely because she was aware of our discomfort, she had a second chance to rectify the situation, and she didn't. In fact, she wasn't even the one who ultimately came to collect the payment.

We weren't expecting any special treatment, just better handling of the situation and a little more consideration for customers who were still eating and drinking.

We won't be back.

It's a shame that an experience like this tarnishes so many years of coming to a place we've always loved.

We came to the restaurant and immediately noticed several empty tables inside and on the terrace. We simply asked if we could sit at one of them, but were told very rudely that they were all reserved, even though there were no reservation signs.

We were with a baby and just wanted to have a quick dinner because we were exhausted after travelling. We politely asked them to check the system and possibly offer us one table, but the waiter was extremely rude and practically shouted at us. I then checked the restaurant’s website and found several available tables, so I made a reservation online while literally standing outside the restaurant.

When I went back inside and said that I had a reservation, they tried to interrupt me and tell me to leave before I could even explain. Thankfully, the bartender eventually checked the system and handled the situation professionally.

During the order, we also specifically asked if all our food could be brought together because our baby was tired and going to bed soon, and we didn’t want to stay long. Our request was completely ignored because they said they have their own rules and everyone has to follow them.

We respect the traditions and culture of different countries, and people can enjoy their food however they like. But when a customer comes to a restaurant, pays for their food and makes a simple request to have everything served together, I don’t think this is unreasonable. Customers should have the choice of whether they want to eat their food together or separately.

We waited 1.5 hours for a steak that takes around 4 minutes to cook. The restaurant was not even particularly busy — the delay was simply because of the way they choose to serve food.

The staff were extremely rude, inflexible and unprofessional, and seemed completely unwilling to listen to the customer.
